headline: Neighbors of 10 Hudson Road ask city to revoke building permits and stop blasting until checks are done.
summary: Public speakers said the lot was deemed unbuildable in 1990 and that its building permit has a $0 line item for fire suppression. They also raised concerns about trees estimated at 50 to 100 years old, ledge blasting, and flooding. The city's electricity aggregation plan is under a 30-day public review that ends November 23rd. The council also approved a marijuana equity ordinance, a letter supporting Senate Bill S457, and a retiree cost-of-living increase, and accepted two grants.
decisions: Approved accepting a $14,000 Massachusetts Cultural Council grant, 8-0, one absent.
Approved accepting a $24,476 Municipal Road Safety grant, 8-0, one absent.
Approved raising the retiree cost-of-living base from $14,000 to $15,000, 8-0, one absent.
Motion to reconsider the retiree cost-of-living increase failed, 0 in favor, 8 opposed, one absent.
Approved accepting the Planning and Development report on National Grid pole and underground utility petitions, 8-0, one absent.
Approved amending city ordinances to add marijuana retail equity standards, 8-0, one absent.
Approved a council letter supporting Senate Bill S457, the Middle School Innovation Fund, 8-0, one absent.
discussion: 10 Hudson Road permits: Public speakers asked the city to audit records, check the trees, and require pre-blast surveys before work continues. They said the lot was deemed unbuildable in 1990 and that a $7,900 betterment fee was not adjusted for inflation.

Electricity aggregation program: The Good Energy representative said community savings since launch through September are over $21 million. The city plans a new contract bid in March, April, or May, and residents will get a notice of any new rates.
Retiree cost-of-living increase: A member asked whether retirees would receive a bigger pension payment, and the answer was yes. Debate then turned to a motion to reconsider, which failed.
Middle school innovation fund: A member asked how many schools would compete for the grant. The answer was not known, and members said Senator Tarr would be asked.

Marijuana equity ordinance: The general counsel said the state requires a social equity plan. The ordinance is a model from the Cannabis Control Commission and gives the city a presumption of compliance.
